name: Stonks
blurb: Meme Man, a smooth 3D head, in front of a rising market chart captioned "STONKS"
title: Stonks Meme: Meaning, Origin & Meme Man
description: Stonks is a deliberately misspelled "stocks" meme showing Meme Man before a rising chart, posted by the Facebook page Special Meme Fresh on 5 June 2017.
h1: What does the Stonks meme mean?
answer: Stonks is a meme of Meme Man, a bald, smooth, pale 3D-rendered head, pasted onto a man in a suit in front of a rising stock-market chart, with the caption "STONKS", a deliberate misspelling of "stocks". The Facebook page Special Meme Fresh posted it on 5 June 2017, and it spread on Reddit and Twitter. People use it to mock bad financial or life decisions as if they were genius moves, and "not stonks" for when things go down.

body: Meme Man is a crude, pale 3D-rendered head with blue eyes and a blank expression. In Stonks he is pasted onto a stock photo of a man in a business suit with his arms crossed, standing in front of a chart that is trending upwards. The word "STONKS" sits underneath in plain letters.
The humour is in the deliberate dumbness: the misspelling and the cheap 3D head make fun of people who think they are financial geniuses.

head: Date
Event
rows: Meme Man starts appearing as a recurring character on the surreal Facebook meme page Special Meme Fresh.
Special Meme Fresh posts the "Stonks" image on 5 June; in July it reaches Reddit.
Stonks becomes a common reaction image and text joke on Reddit and Twitter, with edits like "not stonks".
During the GameStop share frenzy, Reddit's r/wallstreetbets users make Meme Man the face of "stonks".
Fortnite releases Diamond Hanz, an outfit based on Meme Man, as an April Fools' joke.

ul: Mock-smart decisions: "Spent all my savings on snacks so I can't spend it on anything worse. Stonks."
"Not stonks": a frowning Meme Man with the numbers going down, for when something goes badly.
Typing "stonks" as a one-word reaction to any small win.
Sibling misspellings from the same surreal-meme world: "helth", "mafs", "stronk", and Meme Man getting "ANGERY" at vegetables ("vegetals").

body: Stonks is a classic that is still widely understood, especially in comments about money, prices or questionable deals. The word has become general slang on its own: many people say "stonks" without ever showing the picture. It is used almost entirely as a joke, not as real financial talk.

faq.a: It is a deliberate misspelling of "stocks", to make the character sound clueless while acting like a financial genius.

faq.q: Who is the guy in the Stonks meme?
faq.a: Meme Man, a smooth 3D head used since 2014 by the Facebook page Special Meme Fresh in surreal memes.
The opposite: something lost value or went badly, often shown with the arrow pointing down.
